title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the surrounding pages: Grothendieck is computing the genus-0, three-point building block S_0T_{0,I} of the Teichmüller tower, with I a 3-element set (I ∈ Ob Ens_3). The previous page identifies it, as a Z^I-groupoid, with Σ_I(or(I)). Here or(I) is the two-element μ2-torsor of orientations (cyclic orders) of I. Σ_I is an extension 0→Z^I→Σ_I→{±1}→0, eq. (13). For any extension 0→π→Σ→γ→0 and γ-torsor ε, the π-groupoid Σ(ε) has objects ε and arrows (u,x) with composition (u,x)∘(v,x')=(uv,x') (built on the previous page).

Step 1. Σ_I is the pullback of the extension (S_I) = (S)^I. Here (S) is the canonical extension 0→Z→R→U→0 (U = circle group, R its universal cover). The pullback is taken along the homomorphism (4) {±1}=μ2→U^I. Geometrically: the Dehn twists around the three boundary circles, plus the lift of rotation by π in each tangent circle.

Step 2. Factor (4) as μ2 --diag--> μ2^I → U^I, as in (5).

Step 3. Pulling (S) back along μ2⊂U gives 0→Z→(1/2)Z→μ2→0. This is canonically isomorphic to the standard extension (K1): 0→Z --2--> Z→Z/2Z≅μ2→0.

Step 4. Take the I-th cartesian power of (K1); this is the pullback of (S_I) along μ2^I→U^I. Then pull back along the diagonal μ2→μ2^I.

Step 5. Use the morphism of extensions (diag, diag, diag) from (K1) to (K1)^I. It shows that the same extension is also the pushout of (K1) along the diagonal Z→Z^I. This is eq. (15) on the next page.

Concretely, Σ_I ≅ {m ∈ Z^I : all m_i have the same parity}. The kernel Z^I sits inside via multiplication by 2. The next page draws the consequence: Hom(x,y) = Z^I if x=y and Imp^I (odd integers) if x≠y. This gives a complete algebraic, S_I-compatible description of the genus-0 three-point Teichmüller groupoid with its 'two hemispheres' as objects. Topologically, the non-trivial arrow is the π-rotation of the pair of pants exchanging its two sides. Its square is the product of the three boundary Dehn twists (the element (1,1,1) after rescaling).
errors: No mathematical error. The page computes the pullback along diag: μ2→μ2^I, while the conclusion on the next page is phrased as a pushout along diag: Z→Z^I. These agree by the morphism of extensions drawn at the bottom. The isomorphism is (a,k)↦2a+k·(1,…,1) from the pushout Z^I⊕Z/Z to {m: all m_i ≡ same mod 2}; it is correct.

Worth noting, though not stated on the page: Σ_I is torsion-free, so the extension (13) is non-split. The π-rotation does not lift to an involution once boundary twists are taken into account. The computation is consistent with this.

ideas.what: Pullback of the universal-cover extension 0→Z→R→U→0 along μ2⊂U gives the standard extension 0→Z--2-->Z→Z/2→0.

Description of the genus-0, 3-point Teichmüller groupoid (pair of pants with tangential structure): objects = the two orientations of I; Hom(x,x)=Z^I (boundary twists); Hom(x,y)=Imp^I (odd half-twist lifts).
ideas.modern_name: Pair-of-pants building block of the Teichmüller (Lego) groupoid / half-twist relation in the mapping class group of the pair of pants
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, Esquisse d'un programme (1984), in outline; worked out by Moore–Seiberg, Bakalov–Kirillov, Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Funar–Gelca
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the genus-0 building blocks of the Teichmüller tower in general terms; this explicit extension computation is not there as far as I know.

ideas.what: The non-split extension 0→Z^I→Σ_I→μ2→0 realised as the pushout of (K1) along diag: Z→Z^I, equivalently as the 'all coordinates of equal parity' sublattice of Z^I.
ideas.modern_name: Pushout of extensions; framed or tangential mapping class group of the 3-holed sphere

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine computation of an extension of μ2 by Z^I. It serves to describe the genus-0, three-point block of the Teichmüller groupoid. The result (half-twist squared = product of boundary twists, two-object groupoid) is well known in the Lego–Teichmüller literature. It is of interest only as documentation of Grothendieck's working method.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'Je vais donner une description lgs [?] plus simple' — the unclear word is probably 'un peu' or a similar intensifier. The small 'μ2' written above belongs to the brace under {±1} in line 2, not to this line.
Line 4: 'en factorisant [-...-] par comme dans (5)' — a struck word is replaced by 'factorisant'. The intended sense is 'en factorisant (4), comme dans (5)'.
'[-extension-] qui est connue [?] comme [?] l'ext standard' — most likely reads 'qui est canoniquement isomorphe à l'ext standard'.
